notices.short_title: FY27 New Contract   NY 15/15 Congregate Supportive Housing
notices.description:
In November 2015 Mayor Bill de Blasio announced the NYC Supportive Housing Initiative to fund and develop 15,000 new units of supportive housing in New York City over the next fifteen years. This far reaching and comprehensive initiative targets the most vulnerable homeless New Yorkers in need of supportive housing. Supportive housing combines affordable housing with appropriate social services to help special populations, including individuals and families with serious mental (SMI) illness and substance use disorders (SUD). 
Provision of Congregate Supportive Housing for SA at 160 Van Cortlandt Park South, Bronx, NY 10463. Round 25.

notices.description:
The New York City Department of Transportation (NYCDOT) Division of Bridges seeks to procure and install Bridge Grid Deck Panels at the Grand Street Bridge, and has received approval from the New York City Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) to use a Competitive Negotiated Acquisition (NA) pursuant to Section 3-04(b)(2)(ii) and Section 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules (PPB) Rules, as there are a limited number of vendors available and able to perform the work and it is not practical or advantageous to award a contract for these services by competitive sealed bidding or competitive sealed proposal.

These systems must meet the performance, durability, and fabrication quality requirements defined by the BGFMA, which sets nationally recognized benchmarks for heavy-duty applications such as movable bridges, port facilities, and t…

Date: Wednesday, December 9, 2026 
Time: 6 PM 8 PM

Register To Participate in the Conversation

notices.short_title: NOTICE OF RATIFICATION OF A MINOR RULES VIOLATION
notices.description:
On November 18, 2026, pursuant to Section 1-02(h)(1)(ii) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) ratified a Minor Rules Violation request submitted by the New York City Department of Probation (DOP) in connection with the Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) for the NYCHA Neighborhood Employment Services Program.

The violation concerned compliance with PPB Rule §2-11, as the public notice and comment process was conducted after the proposed contract commencement date of March 1, 2025. The public notice was published on April 16, 2026, with comments accepted through April 29, 2026. DOP also republished the Notice of Intent to reflect the revised contract term and amount.

DOP determined that the procedural violation had no significant adverse impact on the procurement process or its intended outcome, and that ratification is in the best interests of the City. The ratification allows DOP to proceed with the remaining contract approval and registration requirements.

The New York City Department of Transportation (NYCDOT) Division of Bridges seeks to procure and install Bridge Grid Deck Panels at the Grand Street Bridge, and has received approval from the New York City Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) to use a Competitive Negotiated Acquisition (NA) pursuant to Section 3-04(b)(2)(ii) and Section 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules (PPB) Rules, as there are a limited number of vendors available and able to perform the work and it is not practical or advantageous to award a contract for these services by competitive sealed bidding or competitive sealed proposal. 

The Division follows established industry standards in the use of open and partially filled steel grid decking systems for movable and fixed bridges. These systems must meet the performance, durability, and fabrication quality requirements defined by the BGFMA, which sets nationally recognized benchmarks for heavy-duty applications such as movable bridges, port facilities, and t…
notable.plain: The Department of Transportation intends to award a negotiated contract, with a response deadline of Dec. 9, 2027, to procure and install bridge grid deck panels at the Grand Street Bridge, citing a limited number of capable vendors.
